components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — coarse grain, hence rough; also in 粉 powder, 粮 grain.
且 (qiě) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 租 zū and 阻 zǔ.

example.hanzi: 这根绳子很粗。
example.pinyin: Zhè gēn shéngzi hěn cū.
example.english: This rope is very thick.
example.fact: 粗 describes thick round things and coarse textures (opposite of 细): 粗糙 (rough), 粗粮 (whole grains), 粗茶淡饭 (simple food). It also means careless or rude: 粗心 (careless), 粗鲁 (crude).

examples.hanzi: 他的手指很粗，也很有力。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒuzhǐ hěn cū, yě hěn yǒulì.
examples.english: His hands are thick and big.

examples.hanzi: 别粗心，再检查一遍。
examples.pinyin: Bié cūxīn, zài jiǎnchá yí biàn.
examples.english: Don't be careless, and check once more.

components.note: 罒 (net, 网 variant) — marks nets and covers, as in 罗, 罚; 罩 is a cover or a basket net, as in 胸罩 bra.
卓 (zhuó) — only a loose sound hint (zhào vs zhuó).

example.hanzi: 出门要戴口罩。
example.pinyin: Chūmén yào dài kǒuzhào.
example.english: You need to wear a mask when you go out.
example.fact: 罩 is a cover: 口罩 (face mask), 灯罩 (lampshade), 罩衫 (smock). As a verb, it also means to cover or to look after: in slang 我罩你 is "I've got your back."

examples.hanzi: 冬天出门最好戴上耳罩。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān chūmén zuìhǎo dàishàng ěrzhào.
examples.english: In winter it is best to wear earmuffs when going out.

examples.hanzi: 台灯上有一个红色的灯罩。
examples.pinyin: Táidēng shàng yǒu yí ge hóngsè de dēngzhào.
examples.english: There is a red lampshade on the desk lamp.

components.note: 串 (chuàn) — two pieces strung on a line 丨: a skewer or string, as in 羊肉串 lamb skewer and 一串 a string.

example.hanzi: 我想吃一串烤肉。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī yí chuàn kǎoròu.
example.english: I want to eat a skewer of grilled meat.
example.fact: 串 is a measure word for things strung together: 一串钥匙, 一串葡萄. 羊肉串 (lamb skewers) are a popular street food, and 串门 means to drop in on a neighbour. 串通 means to collude.

examples.hanzi: 她手上戴着一串珍珠。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒu shàng dài zhe yí chuàn zhēnzhū.
examples.english: She is wearing a string of pearls on her wrist.

examples.hanzi: 桌上放着一串葡萄。
examples.pinyin: Zhuō shàng fàng zhe yí chuàn pútao.
examples.english: There is a bunch of grapes on the table.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting; also in 分 divide, 切 cut.
前 (qián) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 煎 jiān.
刀 — the picture of a knife blade; as 刂 on the right it marks cutting, as in 别, 利, 剪.

example.hanzi: 她用剪刀剪断了绳子。
example.pinyin: tā yòng jiǎndāo jiǎnduànle shéngzi.
example.english: She cut the rope with scissors.
example.fact: The earliest scissors, found in Mesopotamia roughly 3,000 years ago, were spring-action tools made from a single strip of bronze bent into two blades that snapped shut. The pivoted, cross-bladed design familiar today, with a fixed pin joining two separate blades, was a later Roman innovation that appeared around 100 CE.

examples.hanzi: 请借我一把剪刀。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiè wǒ yì bǎ jiǎndāo.
examples.english: Please lend me a pair of scissors.

examples.hanzi: 孩子还太小，不能自己用剪刀。
examples.pinyin: Háizi hái tài xiǎo, bù néng zìjǐ yòng jiǎndāo.
examples.english: The child is still too young to use scissors alone.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 周末我们全家去饭馆吃点心。
example.pinyin: zhōumò wǒmen quánjiā qù fànguǎn chī diǎnxin.
example.english: On the weekend our whole family goes to a restaurant to eat dim sum.
example.fact: Dim sum's tradition of small dishes eaten alongside tea, known as 'yum cha,' is believed to have grown out of roadside teahouses along the ancient Silk Road, where travelers stopped to rest their horses and were served tea with light snacks — a custom Cantonese culture later refined into today's elaborate multi-course tea brunch.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢下午茶配一份小点心。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan xiàwǔchá pèi yí fèn xiǎo diǎnxin.
examples.english: I like having a small snack with afternoon tea.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶做的点心又香又甜。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zuò de diǎnxin yòu xiāng yòu tián.
examples.english: The pastries Grandma makes are fragrant and sweet.

components.note: 上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.hanzi: 钥匙卡住了,打不开门。
example.pinyin: yàoshi kǎzhùle, dǎ bù kāi mén.
example.english: The key got stuck, and the door won't open.
example.fact: In March 2021, the container ship Ever Given ran aground and wedged sideways across the Suez Canal, blocking one of the world's busiest shipping lanes for six days. The jam held up an estimated $9.6 billion in trade every single day it remained stuck, rippling through global supply chains for months afterward.

examples.hanzi: 一块骨头卡住了他的喉咙。
examples.pinyin: Yí kuài gǔtou kǎzhù le tā de hóulóng.
examples.english: A bone got stuck in his throat.

examples.hanzi: 拉链卡住了，拉不上去。
examples.pinyin: Lāliàn kǎzhù le, lā bu shàngqù.
examples.english: The zipper is jammed and won't go up.

components.note: 气 (gas, air) — marks gases, as in 氢 hydrogen, 氮 nitrogen.
羊 (yáng) gives a close sound; 养 yǎng shares it and sounds exactly like 氧.
气 (air, vapor) — lines of rising vapor or breath. Add water for 汽 steam; seen in 生气 get angry, 空气 air.

example.hanzi: 医生给病人吸上了氧气。
example.pinyin: yīshēng gěi bìngrén xīshàngle yǎngqì.
example.english: The doctor put the patient on oxygen.
example.fact: Earth's atmosphere was not always oxygen-rich — for roughly the first two billion years of the planet's history it contained almost none. Photosynthesizing cyanobacteria slowly changed that during the Great Oxidation Event around 2.4 billion years ago, a shift so severe it wiped out most of the anaerobic life that had dominated until then.

examples.hanzi: 这个房间太闷了，缺少氧气。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān tài mēn le, quēshǎo yǎngqì.
examples.english: This room is too stuffy and lacks oxygen.

examples.hanzi: 植物通过光合作用产生氧气。
examples.pinyin: Zhíwù tōngguò guānghé zuòyòng chǎnshēng yǎngqì.
examples.english: Plants produce oxygen through photosynthesis.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 遗 is leaving something behind or losing it.
贵 (valuable) — what is precious is what you regret leaving behind or what is left to heirs.
亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.

example.hanzi: 这种疾病可能通过基因遗传给后代。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng jíbìng kěnéng tōngguò jīyīn yíchuán gěi hòudài.
example.english: This disease can be genetically inherited by future generations.
example.fact: Gregor Mendel, an Austrian monk, spent eight years in the 1850s and 1860s cross-breeding thousands of pea plants in his monastery garden, tracking traits like flower color and seed shape across generations. His statistical patterns, largely ignored during his lifetime, were rediscovered around 1900 and became the foundation of modern genetics.

examples.hanzi: 他的蓝眼睛是遗传自妈妈的。
examples.pinyin: Tā de lán yǎnjing shì yíchuán zì māma de.
examples.english: He inherited his blue eyes from his mother.

examples.hanzi: 这种特点是由遗传决定的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng tèdiǎn shì yóu yíchuán juédìng de.
examples.english: This trait is determined by heredity.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 抽 is to pull out.
由 (yóu) — near sound — 抽 is chōu; 由 also sounds out 油 yóu and 邮 yóu.
尸 (body, shelter) — often a building or cover: 屋 house, 层 storey, 居 dwell. In 屉 it suggests a shelter, such as a drawer or tray in a case.
世 (shì) — probably a loose sound clue for tì, but not certain. Memory aid: a drawer (抽屉) is a tier that slides in and out of a world of its own.

example.hanzi: 他把文件放进了抽屉里。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ wénjiàn fàng jìnle chōuti lǐ.
example.english: He put the documents into the drawer.
example.fact: The modern drawer with smooth ball-bearing slides is a surprisingly recent invention — it did not become common in furniture until the mid-20th century. Before that, drawers ran on plain wood-to-wood friction, which is why old dressers so often stick or need to be pulled at an angle to open.

examples.hanzi: 你的钥匙在第二个抽屉里。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de yàoshi zài dì èr ge chōuti lǐ.
examples.english: Your keys are in the second drawer.

examples.hanzi: 他拉开抽屉，拿出了一支笔。
examples.pinyin: Tā lākāi chōuti, ná chū le yì zhī bǐ.
examples.english: He pulled open the drawer and took out a pen.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree 木 boxed in by an enclosure 囗: trapped, hemmed in; hence 困难 difficulty.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth and land, as in 地, 城, 块; 境 is a stretch of land, a border or condition.
竟 (jìng) — same sound — 境 is jìng, like 竟; 竟 also sounds out 镜 jìng.

example.hanzi: 公司目前陷入了财务困境。
example.pinyin: gōngsī mùqián xiànrùle cáiwù kùnjìng.
example.english: The company is currently caught in a financial predicament.
example.fact: The prisoner's dilemma, one of the most famous predicaments in game theory, was formalized in 1950 by mathematicians Merrill Flood and Melvin Dresher at the RAND Corporation while researching nuclear strategy. It shows how two rational people acting purely in self-interest can end up worse off than if they had cooperated.

examples.hanzi: 他们现在陷入了经济困境。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen xiànzài xiànrù le jīngjì kùnjìng.
examples.english: They have now fallen into financial difficulty.

examples.hanzi: 她帮朋友走出了困境。
examples.pinyin: Tā bāng péngyou zǒuchū le kùnjìng.
examples.english: She helped her friend out of a predicament.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸 — 绪 first meant the end of a thread, then the clue, as in 头绪, and mood, as in 情绪.
者 (zhě) — loose hint — 绪 is xù.

example.hanzi: 这个案子毫无头绪。
example.pinyin: zhège ànzi háowú tóuxù.
example.english: This case has no leads at all.
example.fact: Forensic science largely rests on Locard's exchange principle, formulated by French criminologist Edmond Locard around 1910: every person who enters a crime scene both brings something into it and takes something away, however microscopic — a principle that underlies modern fiber, fingerprint, and DNA analysis.

examples.hanzi: 我想了很久，还是理不出头绪。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng le hěn jiǔ, háishi lǐ bù chū tóuxù.
examples.english: I thought for a long time but still couldn't sort out the main thread.

examples.hanzi: 他讲得很乱，大家听不出头绪。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎng de hěn luàn, dàjiā tīng bù chū tóuxù.
examples.english: He spoke so messily that nobody could follow it.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.
土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 坏; 压 is earth pressed down under a cliff 厂.

example.hanzi: 医生每天都要给病人测血压。
example.pinyin: yīshēng měitiān dōu yào gěi bìngrén cè xuèyā.
example.english: The doctor measures the patient's blood pressure every day.
example.fact: Giraffes have the highest blood pressure of any mammal, roughly two to three times that of humans, because their hearts must pump blood nearly two meters up their long necks to reach the brain. Thick, elastic vessel walls and a tight sheath of skin around their lower legs keep this pressure from causing swelling when they lower their heads to drink.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷的血压有点儿高。
examples.pinyin: Yéye de xuèyā yǒudiǎnr gāo.
examples.english: Grandpa's blood pressure is a little high.

examples.hanzi: 少吃盐有助于控制血压。
examples.pinyin: Shǎo chī yán yǒuzhù yú kòngzhì xuèyā.
examples.english: Eating less salt helps control blood pressure.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — marks bamboo and things made of it, as in 笔, 筷, 篮; 箭 is an arrow, shaft of bamboo.
前 (qián) hints at the sound: 箭 jiàn is close to 剪 jiǎn and 煎 jiān.

example.hanzi: 他拉弓射出一支箭。
example.pinyin: Tā lā gōng shè chū yì zhī jiàn.
example.english: He drew his bow and shot an arrow.
example.fact: 箭 is counted with 支 or 根. It makes 弓箭 (bow and arrow), 火箭 (rocket, "fire arrow"), 箭头 (arrowhead). The idiom 归心似箭 compares a longing to get home to a flying arrow.

examples.hanzi: 他射出的箭正中靶心。
examples.pinyin: Tā shèchū de jiàn zhèng zhòng bǎxīn.
examples.english: The arrow he shot hit the bullseye.

examples.hanzi: 路边的箭头指向出口。
examples.pinyin: Lù biān de jiàntóu zhǐxiàng chūkǒu.
examples.english: The arrow on the roadside points to the exit.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 嚼 is chewing.
爵 (jué) — close sound: 嚼 jiáo/jué.

example.hanzi: 吃东西要细嚼慢咽。
example.pinyin: Chī dōngxi yào xìjiáo mànyàn.
example.english: You should chew your food slowly and thoroughly.
example.fact: 嚼 is to chew, read jiáo in speech and jué in 咀嚼 (jǔjué). 细嚼慢咽 is the standard advice for healthy eating, and 嚼舌根 means to gossip, "chewing the tongue root."

examples.hanzi: 你嚼一嚼，看看味道怎么样。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiáo yi jiáo, kànkan wèidào zěnmeyàng.
examples.english: Chew it and see how it tastes.

examples.hanzi: 他一边走一边嚼口香糖。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìbiān zǒu yìbiān jiáo kǒuxiāngtáng.
examples.english: He chews gum as he walks.

components.note: 十 (ten) — a cross: first a single vertical line, later crossed with a horizontal bar. Seen in 十分, 二十, and in 千.
足 (foot) — a kneecap 口 above a foot 止; as the radical ⻊ it marks feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路, 踢. Also means enough.

example.hanzi: 他对这次比赛信心十足。
example.pinyin: tā duì zhè cì bǐsài xìnxīn shízú.
example.english: He is fully confident about this competition.
example.fact: Roughly 90% of the world's languages use a base-10 (decimal) counting system, almost certainly because humans have ten fingers to count on. A notable exception is the ancient Maya, who developed a base-20 system, likely by counting fingers and toes together.

examples.hanzi: 这道汤的味道十足，一点儿也不淡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào tāng de wèidào shízú, yìdiǎnr yě bú dàn.
examples.english: This soup is full of flavor and not bland at all.

examples.hanzi: 她是个十足的乐天派。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge shízú de lètiānpài.
examples.english: She is a thoroughgoing optimist.

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 她刚办了健身房的会员卡。
example.pinyin: tā gāng bànle jiànshēnfáng de huìyuán kǎ.
example.english: She just got a membership card for the gym.
example.fact: The Royal Society, founded in London in 1660, is the oldest continuously existing national scientific institution in the world. Its early fellows included Isaac Newton and Robert Boyle, and to this day new members are still inducted by signing the same charter book used since the society's founding.

examples.hanzi: 办会员可以享受八折优惠。
examples.pinyin: Bàn huìyuán kěyǐ xiǎngshòu bā zhé yōuhuì.
examples.english: Becoming a member gets you 20% off.

examples.hanzi: 这家书店的会员每月能借五本书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shūdiàn de huìyuán měi yuè néng jiè wǔ běn shū.
examples.english: Members of this bookstore can borrow five books a month.

components.note: 长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.

example.hanzi: 长期熬夜对身体不好。
example.pinyin: chángqī áoyè duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
example.english: Staying up late for a long time is bad for your health.
example.fact: The Broadbalk Wheat Experiment at Rothamsted Research in England has been running continuously since 1843, making it the longest-running agricultural field experiment in the world. Researchers have tracked the same plots' soil and crop yields under different fertilizer treatments for more than 180 years.

examples.hanzi: 这位病人需要长期治疗。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi bìngrén xūyào chángqī zhìliáo.
examples.english: This patient needs long-term treatment.

examples.hanzi: 他们已经长期没有联系了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yǐjīng chángqī méiyǒu liánxì le.
examples.english: They haven't been in touch for a long time.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.

example.hanzi: 他家养了一只可爱的拉拉。
example.pinyin: tā jiā yǎngle yī zhī kě'ài de lālā.
example.english: His family keeps an adorable Labrador retriever.
example.fact: Despite the name, Labrador retrievers did not originate in Labrador but in Newfoundland, Canada, where fishermen bred them in the 1700s to retrieve fish and haul nets from the icy North Atlantic waters. British aristocrats imported the breed in the 19th century and refined it into the dog known today.

examples.hanzi: 拉拉每天早上都要出去散步。
examples.pinyin: Lālā měi tiān zǎoshang dōu yào chūqù sànbù.
examples.english: Lala has to go out for a walk every morning.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们拉拉手，围成了一个圈。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen lālā shǒu, wéi chéng le yí ge quān.
examples.english: The kids held hands and formed a circle.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 木 is a tree, as in 树, 桌, 林; 朵 is a cluster hanging from a branch, the measure word for flowers and clouds.

example.hanzi: 花园里开了一朵红花。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ kāi le yì duǒ hóng huā.
example.english: A red flower has bloomed in the garden.
example.fact: 朵 counts flowers and clouds: 一朵花, 一朵云. 花朵 means a blossom, and 耳朵 (ear) also contains 朵, read with a neutral tone: ěrduo.

examples.hanzi: 天上飘着几朵白云。
examples.pinyin: Tiān shàng piāo zhe jǐ duǒ báiyún.
examples.english: A few white clouds are drifting in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 她耳朵很灵，什么都听得见。
examples.pinyin: Tā ěrduo hěn líng, shénme dōu tīng de jiàn.
examples.english: She has sharp ears and can hear everything.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 他明年就要上中学了。
example.pinyin: tā míngnián jiù yào shàng zhōngxué le.
example.english: He will start middle school next year.
example.fact: Eton College in England, founded by King Henry VI in 1440, has operated continuously as a secondary school for over 580 years, making it one of the oldest schools in the world still teaching students today.

examples.hanzi: 我的弟弟在读中学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de dìdi zài dú zhōngxué.
examples.english: My younger brother is in middle school.

examples.hanzi: 中学的课程比小学难得多。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngxué de kèchéng bǐ xiǎoxué nán de duō.
examples.english: Middle school courses are much harder than primary school ones.

components.note: 勹 (to wrap) — wraps around 厶, like a hook curling round something. Memory aid, not a proven origin.
厶 (small, private) — the tucked-in part. 勾 is the sound part of 沟 gōu ditch, 钩 gōu hook, 构 gòu build, with hook-like meaning in 勾引.
弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.

example.hanzi: 广告常常用美食图片勾引消费者购买。
example.pinyin: guǎnggào chángcháng yòng měishí túpiàn gōuyǐn xiāofèizhě gòumǎi.
example.english: Advertisements often use pictures of delicious food to tempt consumers into buying.
example.fact: Deep-sea anglerfish dangle a bioluminescent lure, called an esca, above their mouths to attract curious prey in the pitch-black ocean depths. The light comes from colonies of symbiotic bacteria living inside the lure, which the anglerfish cannot produce on its own.

examples.hanzi: 别被网上的广告勾引了，不要乱买东西。
examples.pinyin: Bié bèi wǎng shàng de guǎnggào gōuyǐn le, bú yào luàn mǎi dōngxi.
examples.english: Don't be tempted by online ads and buy things at random.

examples.hanzi: 香味勾引着路过的人走进了面包店。
examples.pinyin: Xiāngwèi gōuyǐn zhe lùguò de rén zǒujìn le miànbāodiàn.
examples.english: The aroma lured passers-by into the bakery.

components.note: 此 (cǐ) is a sound clue for 紫 zǐ, 雌 cí and 些 xiē; as a word it means "this".
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 领导表示会认真调查此事。
example.pinyin: lǐngdǎo biǎoshì huì rènzhēn diàochá cǐshì.
example.english: The leader said they would seriously investigate this matter.
example.fact: The official investigations into the 1912 sinking of the Titanic led directly to the first International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) in 1914, which mandated lifeboat space for every passenger and round-the-clock radio watches. Updated versions of that same treaty still govern maritime safety worldwide today.

examples.hanzi: 此事与你无关，请不要多问。
examples.pinyin: Cǐ shì yǔ nǐ wúguān, qǐng bú yào duō wèn.
examples.english: This matter has nothing to do with you, so please don't ask more.

examples.hanzi: 我们会尽快处理此事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huì jǐnkuài chùlǐ cǐ shì.
examples.english: We will handle this matter as soon as possible.

components.note: 工 (tool, work) — originally a carpenter's square held in a hand — the same word as 矩; 巨 also sounds out 距 jù and 拒 jù.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 传说中山里住着一个巨人。
example.pinyin: chuánshuō zhōng shānlǐ zhùzhe yī gè jùrén.
example.english: According to legend, a giant lives in the mountains.
example.fact: Robert Wadlow, born in Illinois in 1918, is the tallest person ever reliably recorded at 8 feet 11 inches (2.72 meters). His extraordinary growth was caused by a pituitary tumor that continuously released growth hormone; he was still growing when he died at age 22.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的巨人有一双大脚。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de jùrén yǒu yì shuāng dà jiǎo.
examples.english: The giant in the story has a pair of huge feet.

examples.hanzi: 他身材高大，像个巨人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēncái gāodà, xiàng ge jùrén.
examples.english: He is tall and big, like a giant.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — carrying by hand; also in 拿 take, 提 carry.
巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.

example.hanzi: 出国旅行时请随身携带护照。
example.pinyin: chūguó lǚxíng shí qǐng suíshēn xiédài hùzhào.
example.english: When traveling abroad, please carry your passport with you.
example.fact: A camel's hump doesn't store water, as commonly believed — it stores fat, which the animal can convert into energy and metabolic water during long desert crossings. This adaptation lets a camel carry a heavy load and go without drinking for over a week in extreme heat.

examples.hanzi: 飞机上不能携带太大的行李。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī shàng bù néng xiédài tài dà de xíngli.
examples.english: You can't carry overly large luggage on the plane.

examples.hanzi: 这个小包很轻，方便携带。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo bāo hěn qīng, fāngbiàn xiédài.
examples.english: This small bag is light and easy to carry.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 急 is a heart in a hurry. The top is a variant of 及 (jí, reach), the same sound as in 级 and 极.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.

example.hanzi: 学校组织了一次急救培训课程。
example.pinyin: xuéxiào zǔzhīle yī cì jíjiù péixùn kèchéng.
example.english: The school organized a first-aid training course.
example.fact: Modern CPR as taught today was developed in the late 1950s and early 1960s by physicians Peter Safar and James Elam, who combined mouth-to-mouth ventilation with chest compressions into a single technique. Safar's 1957 book laid the basis for CPR training used worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 他学会了急救，救了一个人的命。
examples.pinyin: Tā xuéhuì le jíjiù, jiù le yí ge rén de mìng.
examples.english: He learned first aid and saved a person's life.

examples.hanzi: 请马上打电话叫急救车。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng mǎshàng dǎ diànhuà jiào jíjiùchē.
examples.english: Please call for an ambulance right away.

components.note: 马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 古代的贵族喜欢乘坐马车出行。
example.pinyin: gǔdài de guìzú xǐhuān chéngzuò mǎchē chūxíng.
example.english: Ancient aristocrats liked to travel by carriage.
example.fact: The earliest wheeled vehicles, dating to around 3500 BCE in Mesopotamia, used solid wooden wheels that were heavy and slow. The lighter spoked wheel wasn't invented until roughly 2000 BCE, and it revolutionized warfare by making fast, maneuverable horse-drawn chariots possible.

examples.hanzi: 马车缓缓地走在石头路上。
examples.pinyin: Mǎchē huǎnhuǎn de zǒu zài shítou lù shàng.
examples.english: The carriage moved slowly along the stone road.

examples.hanzi: 游客们坐马车参观了古城。
examples.pinyin: Yóukèmen zuò mǎchē cānguān le gǔchéng.
examples.english: The tourists toured the old town by horse carriage.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house or shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; a hand 寸 under a roof means guarding.
寸 (hand, inch) — originally a hand, as in 对, 寻, 封.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.

example.hanzi: 士兵们日夜守护着边境。
example.pinyin: shìbīngmen rìyè shǒuhùzhe biānjìng.
example.english: The soldiers guard the border day and night.
example.fact: A 2012 Chinese government survey measured the total length of all sections, branches, and spurs of the Great Wall of China, built and rebuilt over more than two thousand years to guard the northern frontier, at over 21,000 kilometers — more than half the Earth's circumference.

examples.hanzi: 警察日夜守护着这座城市。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá rìyè shǒuhù zhe zhè zuò chéngshì.
examples.english: The police protect this city day and night.

examples.hanzi: 母亲一直守护在孩子的床边。
examples.pinyin: Mǔqīn yìzhí shǒuhù zài háizi de chuángbiān.
examples.english: The mother stayed at her child's bedside the whole time.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 事故的原因目前仍然不明。
example.pinyin: shìgù de yuányīn mùqián réngrán bùmíng.
example.english: The cause of the accident is still unclear at present.
example.fact: Ball lightning — glowing, floating spheres of light reported during thunderstorms for centuries — remains scientifically unexplained. Despite hundreds of eyewitness accounts and several competing hypotheses involving plasma or vaporized silicon, no laboratory experiment has yet reliably reproduced anything matching the reported behavior.

examples.hanzi: 原因不明，请你再检查一下。
examples.pinyin: Yuányīn bù míng, qǐng nǐ zài jiǎnchá yíxià.
examples.english: The cause is unclear, so please check again.

examples.hanzi: 一个不明物体飞过了天空。
examples.pinyin: Yí ge bùmíng wùtǐ fēi guò le tiānkōng.
examples.english: An unidentified object flew across the sky.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — a bird over a flame is scorched. 焦 also sounds out 蕉 jiāo and 礁 jiāo.
灬 (fire, 四点底) — flames at the bottom, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 煮 cook.
心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 虑 is to turn something over in the mind.

example.hanzi: 考试前她感到非常焦虑。
example.pinyin: kǎoshì qián tā gǎndào fēicháng jiāolǜ.
example.english: Before the exam she felt very anxious.
example.fact: Hungarian-Canadian endocrinologist Hans Selye coined the term 'stress' in its modern psychological sense in 1936, describing what he called the 'general adaptation syndrome' — the body's three-stage hormonal response to prolonged threat. His work laid the foundation for later research into cortisol and chronic anxiety.

examples.hanzi: 等医生的结果，我感到很焦虑。
examples.pinyin: Děng yīshēng de jiéguǒ, wǒ gǎndào hěn jiāolǜ.
examples.english: Waiting for the doctor's results, I feel very anxious.

examples.hanzi: 别太焦虑，事情会好起来的。
examples.pinyin: Bié tài jiāolǜ, shìqing huì hǎo qǐlái de.
examples.english: Don't be too anxious, things will get better.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — a cunning beast; also in 猫 cat, 狗 dog.
交 (jiāo) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 较 jiào, 郊 jiāo and 胶 jiāo.
犭 (animal) — a sly beast; also in 猫 cat, 狗 dog.
骨 (gǔ) is a loose clue; 滑 huá shares it and sounds exactly like 猾.

example.hanzi: 狐狸是出了名的狡猾动物。
example.pinyin: húli shì chūle míng de jiǎohuá dòngwù.
example.english: The fox is a famously cunning animal.
example.fact: New Caledonian crows are among the few non-human animals known to manufacture tools rather than just use them, bending twigs into hooks to pull insect larvae from crevices. Ravens go further still, sometimes pretending to hide food in a false spot while a rival watches, only to sneak the real food away once the rival gives up on the decoy.

examples.hanzi: 这个商人很狡猾，你要小心。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shāngrén hěn jiǎohuá, nǐ yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: This merchant is cunning, so be careful.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的狐狸总是很狡猾。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de húli zǒngshì hěn jiǎohuá.
examples.english: The fox in the story is always sly.

meanings: see 海倫市|海伦市[Hai3 lun2 Shi4]

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
亻 (person) — person radical — 伦 is about human relations and order, 伦理 ethics.
仑 (lún) — same sound — 仑 also sounds out 轮 lún and 论 lùn.

example.hanzi: 海伦是我们班新来的交换生。
example.pinyin: Hǎilún shì wǒmen bān xīnlái de jiāohuànshēng.
example.english: Helen is the new exchange student in our class.
example.fact: Helen Keller, who became deaf and blind after an illness at 19 months old, learned to read, write, and speak with the help of her teacher Anne Sullivan. In 1904 she became the first deafblind person to earn a bachelor's degree, graduating cum laude from Radcliffe College.

examples.hanzi: 海伦今年十六岁。
examples.pinyin: Hǎilún jīnnián shíliù suì.
examples.english: Helen is sixteen this year.

examples.hanzi: 我和海伦在图书馆见面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé Hǎilún zài túshūguǎn jiànmiàn.
examples.english: I'm meeting Helen at the library.

meanings: to embezzle by making illegal deductions

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting and sharpness: 利, 别, 到; 刻 is to carve, and the carved marks on a clock became quarter hours.
亥 (hài) is only a loose sound hint; same part in 孩 hái and 核 hé.
艹 (grass) — plant radical, as in 花 flower, 草 grass; 薄 first meant a thicket.
溥 (pǔ) is a loose clue; its right part 尃 also sounds out 博 bó and 簿 bù.

example.hanzi: 他说话总是很刻薄。
example.pinyin: tā shuōhuà zǒngshì hěn kèbó.
example.english: He always speaks harshly.
example.fact: Psychologist John Suler coined the term 'online disinhibition effect' in 2004 to describe why people are often far harsher and blunter in text-based communication than they would ever be face to face — the anonymity, invisibility, and lack of immediate consequence online loosen normal social restraint.

examples.hanzi: 你别这么刻薄，大家都是朋友。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié zhème kèbó, dàjiā dōu shì péngyou.
examples.english: Don't be so mean, we're all friends here.

examples.hanzi: 她刻薄的话让大家都不舒服。
examples.pinyin: Tā kèbó de huà ràng dàjiā dōu bù shūfu.
examples.english: Her harsh words made everyone uncomfortable.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 检 first meant a wooden label or seal.
佥 (qiān) is a close sound clue for jiǎn; also in 验 yàn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 险 xiǎn.
马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.

example.hanzi: 每批产品出厂前都要经过严格检验。
example.pinyin: měi pī chǎnpǐn chūchǎng qián dōu yào jīngguò yángé jiǎnyàn.
example.english: Every batch of products must undergo strict inspection before leaving the factory.
example.fact: The quality-control philosophy known as Six Sigma was developed at Motorola in 1986 by engineer Bill Smith, aiming to reduce manufacturing defects to fewer than 3.4 per million opportunities. The method later spread across global industry after General Electric adopted it company-wide in the mid-1990s under CEO Jack Welch.

examples.hanzi: 医生要检验一下你的血液。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng yào jiǎnyàn yíxià nǐ de xuèyè.
examples.english: The doctor needs to test your blood.

examples.hanzi: 实践是检验真理的标准。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiàn shì jiǎnyàn zhēnlǐ de biāozhǔn.
examples.english: Practice is the test of truth.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
世 (generation) — from 卅 (thirty): about thirty years is one generation, so an age or the world.

example.hanzi: 他的祖父上个月过世了。
example.pinyin: tā de zǔfù shàng gè yuè guòshìle.
example.english: His grandfather passed away last month.
example.fact: Global average life expectancy at birth was only about 32 years in 1900; by 2019 it had more than doubled to over 72 years, one of the most dramatic improvements in human welfare ever recorded, driven mainly by reductions in infant and child mortality rather than people simply living much longer once they reached adulthood.

examples.hanzi: 他的父亲前年过世了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fùqin qiánnián guòshì le.
examples.english: His father passed away the year before last.

examples.hanzi: 老人过世后，家人整理了他的东西。
examples.pinyin: Lǎorén guòshì hòu, jiārén zhěnglǐ le tā de dōngxi.
examples.english: After the old man passed away, his family sorted through his belongings.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and ranks, as in 院, 阶, 防; 阵 is a battle formation.
车 (chariot) — war chariots lined up in rows.

example.hanzi: 外面刮了一阵大风。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn guā le yí zhèn dà fēng.
example.english: A gust of strong wind blew outside.
example.fact: 阵 first meant a battle formation, and still does in 阵容 (lineup) and 上阵 (to go into battle). As a measure word it counts short spells: 一阵风, 一阵雨, 一阵笑声. 一阵子 means "for a while."

examples.hanzi: 刚才下了一阵小雨。
examples.pinyin: Gāngcái xià le yí zhèn xiǎoyǔ.
examples.english: A short spell of light rain just fell.

examples.hanzi: 他笑了一阵，才停下来。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiào le yí zhèn, cái tíng xiàlái.
examples.english: He laughed for a while before stopping.

meanings: Texas (abbr. for 德克薩斯州|德克萨斯州[De2 ke4 sa4 si1 Zhou1])

components.note: 彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.
州 (region) — a river 川 with small islands of land in it; 州 is a region, and also sounds out 洲 zhōu.

example.hanzi: 他去年搬到了德州休斯顿。
example.pinyin: tā qùnián bāndàole Dézhōu Xiūsīdùn.
example.english: He moved to Houston, Texas, last year.
example.fact: Texas is the only U.S. state that was once an independent, internationally recognized nation — the Republic of Texas existed from 1836 to 1845 after winning independence from Mexico, before voluntarily joining the United States as its 28th state.

examples.hanzi: 德州的夏天又长又热。
examples.pinyin: Dézhōu de xiàtiān yòu cháng yòu rè.
examples.english: Summer in Texas is long and hot.

examples.hanzi: 我的朋友在德州开了一家餐厅。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou zài Dézhōu kāi le yì jiā cāntīng.
examples.english: My friend opened a restaurant in Texas.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and talk: 说, 话, 读; a spoken mistake or misunderstanding.
吴 (wú) gives the sound (wù, tone differs); same series 娱 yú and 虞 yú.
角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.

example.hanzi: 她因为误解朋友的话而生气了。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi wùjiě péngyou de huà ér shēngqìle.
example.english: She got angry because she misunderstood her friend's words.
example.fact: Neil Armstrong always insisted he said 'That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind' during the 1969 moon landing, but the crucial word 'a' is inaudible on the recording, leading to decades of debate among audio engineers and linguists about whether it was ever spoken or simply lost to static.

examples.hanzi: 我们之间有一点误解，说清楚就好了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhījiān yǒu yìdiǎn wùjiě, shuō qīngchu jiù hǎo le.
examples.english: There's a bit of a misunderstanding between us, and it'll be fine once we talk it through.

examples.hanzi: 请不要误解我的意思。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào wùjiě wǒ de yìsi.
examples.english: Please don't misunderstand what I mean.

components.note: 金 (metal) — ancient mirrors were bronze, hence 鉴 is a mirror and to examine; as 钅 in 钱 money, 铁 iron.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 鉴于天气恶劣,比赛被迫取消。
example.pinyin: jiànyú tiānqì èliè, bǐsài bèipò qǔxiāo.
example.english: In view of the bad weather, the match was forced to be canceled.
example.fact: Five-day weather forecasts today are as accurate as one-day forecasts were in the 1980s, thanks to satellite data, greater computing power, and improved atmospheric models — a jump that has saved countless lives and dollars by giving communities more advance warning before major storms.

examples.hanzi: 鉴于他的出色表现，公司决定给他升职。
examples.pinyin: Jiànyú tā de chūsè biǎoxiàn, gōngsī juédìng gěi tā shēngzhí.
examples.english: In view of his excellent performance, the company decided to promote him.

examples.hanzi: 鉴于时间有限，我们长话短说。
examples.pinyin: Jiànyú shíjiān yǒuxiàn, wǒmen chánghuà duǎnshuō.
examples.english: Given limited time, let's keep it brief.

components.note: 風 (traditional wind) — 风 is the simplified form of 風, which had 凡 (fán) as a loose sound hint around 虫; the simplified shape is just a reduced form.
日 (sun) — marks light and time, as in 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; the sun over 京 gives a bright scene, hence scenery.
京 (jīng) gives the sound: 景 jǐng is close, as in 影 yǐng and 惊 jīng.

example.hanzi: 站在山顶,风景美得令人窒息。
example.pinyin: zhàn zài shāndǐng, fēngjǐng měi de lìng rén zhìxī.
example.english: Standing on the mountaintop, the scenery is breathtakingly beautiful.
example.fact: The dramatic karst pinnacles of Zhangjiajie National Forest Park in China, shaped over roughly 300 million years by the erosion of quartz-sandstone, directly inspired the floating 'Hallelujah Mountains' in James Cameron's 2009 film Avatar — the park even renamed one of its peaks 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain' afterward.

examples.hanzi: 窗外的风景真好看。
examples.pinyin: Chuāngwài de fēngjǐng zhēn hǎokàn.
examples.english: The scenery outside the window is really beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 我们沿路欣赏了美丽的风景。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yánlù xīnshǎng le měilì de fēngjǐng.
examples.english: We enjoyed the beautiful scenery along the way.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他一下子就把作业写完了。
example.pinyin: tā yīxiàzi jiù bǎ zuòyè xiě wán le.
example.english: He finished his homework in no time.
example.fact: A peregrine falcon can dive at speeds over 240 mph (390 km/h), making it the fastest animal on Earth. A hunting stoop lets it close a gap of several hundred meters in just a few seconds — nature's own version of getting something done in no time.

examples.hanzi: 你别急,一下子说这么多我记不住。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié jí, yīxiàzi shuō zhème duō wǒ jì bú zhù.
examples.english: Don't rush, I can't remember it if you say so much all at once.

examples.hanzi: 窗外一下子下起了大雨。
examples.pinyin: Chuāng wài yīxiàzi xiàqǐle dàyǔ.
examples.english: Suddenly it started pouring outside the window.

components.note: 写 (xiě) — to write; as a part it sounds out 泻 xiè (to flow out).
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 她喜欢写作,每天都写日记。
example.pinyin: tā xǐhuān xiězuò, měitiān dōu xiě rìjì.
example.english: She loves writing, and keeps a diary every day.
example.fact: The oldest known writing system, Sumerian cuneiform, emerged in Mesopotamia around 3400 BCE, originally as wedge-shaped marks pressed into clay to track grain and livestock. It took centuries before the same system was adapted to record stories, laws, and poetry.

examples.hanzi: 我从小就喜欢写作,梦想当作家。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan xiězuò, mèngxiǎng dāng zuòjiā.
examples.english: I've loved writing since I was little and dream of becoming an author.

examples.hanzi: 这门写作课每周有一次作业。
examples.pinyin: Zhè mén xiězuò kè měi zhōu yǒu yí cì zuòyè.
examples.english: This writing course has an assignment every week.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, as in 教, 放, 收; 效 is to imitate or produce results.
交 (jiāo) — near sound — 效 is xiào; 交 also sounds out 校 xiào and 较 jiào.

example.hanzi: 这张票已经过期,无效了。
example.pinyin: zhè zhāng piào yǐjīng guòqī, wúxiào le.
example.english: This ticket has already expired and is no longer valid.
example.fact: In 1938, chemist Roy Plunkett was trying to develop a new refrigerant gas when the compound he produced turned out chemically inert and useless for that purpose. The 'ineffective' substance was Teflon, which went on to become one of the most widely used materials in the world.

examples.hanzi: 这个密码已经无效了,请重新设置。
examples.pinyin: Zhège mìmǎ yǐjīng wúxiào le, qǐng chóngxīn shèzhì.
examples.english: This password is no longer valid, please set a new one.

examples.hanzi: 我跟他说了半天,结果还是无效。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēn tā shuōle bàntiān, jiéguǒ háishi wúxiào.
examples.english: I talked to him for ages, but it was all in vain.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — two hands joined — 共 is doing together; it also sounds out 供 gōng.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 尽管性格不同,他们还是有很多共同点。
example.pinyin: jǐnguǎn xìnggé bùtóng, tāmen háishì yǒu hěn duō gòngtóngdiǎn.
example.english: Despite their different personalities, they still have a lot in common.
example.fact: Dolphins and sharks look strikingly similar — streamlined bodies, dorsal fins, tail flukes — despite dolphins being mammals and sharks being fish that diverged evolutionarily hundreds of millions of years ago. This is a classic case of convergent evolution, where unrelated species independently evolve shared traits because they face the same environmental pressures.

examples.hanzi: 我和我哥哥有很多共同点。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé wǒ gēge yǒu hěn duō gòngtóngdiǎn.
examples.english: My brother and I have a lot in common.

examples.hanzi: 你们两个人有什么共同点吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen liǎng gè rén yǒu shénme gòngtóngdiǎn ma?
examples.english: Do you two have anything in common?

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a person resting on a mat under a roof: to lodge, as in 家 home, 安 peace. Also read xiǔ and xiù.

example.hanzi: 我们学校的宿舍很干净。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào de sùshè hěn gānjìng.
example.english: The dorm at our school is very clean.
example.fact: 宿 as "to lodge" is read sù: 宿舍 (dormitory), 住宿 (accommodation), 露宿 (to sleep outdoors). It has two other readings: xiǔ, counting nights (一宿), and xiù, in 星宿 (constellation).

examples.hanzi: 学生们住在学校的宿舍里。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshēngmen zhù zài xuéxiào de sùshè lǐ.
examples.english: The students live in the school dormitory.

examples.hanzi: 我们在山上露宿了一晚。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài shān shàng lùsù le yì wǎn.
examples.english: We camped out on the mountain for one night.

components.note: 自 (self, nose) — 自 originally pictured a nose — pointing to it meant "me", as in 自己; 鼻 adds 畀 for sound.
畀 (bì) — near sound — 鼻 is bí.

example.hanzi: 我感冒了，鼻子不通气。
example.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, bízi bù tōngqì.
example.english: I have a cold and my nose is blocked.
example.fact: 鼻 is bound in everyday speech as 鼻子. The component 自 is an old picture of a nose, which explains why it came to mean "self." 鼻祖 means a founder, because the nose was thought to form first.

examples.hanzi: 他的鼻子很高。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bízi hěn gāo.
examples.english: He has a high-bridged nose.

examples.hanzi: 我感冒了，一直在流鼻涕。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, yìzhí zài liú bítì.
examples.english: I have a cold and my nose keeps running.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money and value, as in 财, 买, 贵; 贱 is cheap and low in value.
戋 (jiān) — near sound — 贱 is jiàn; 戋 also hints small, as in 钱 and 浅.

example.hanzi: 不要看不起贫贱的人。
example.pinyin: Bùyào kàn bu qǐ pínjiàn de rén.
example.english: Do not look down on poor and lowly people.
example.fact: 贱 is the opposite of 贵 (expensive; noble), so 贵贱 means high and low. It appears in 低贱, 卑贱 and the polite old self-reference 贱姓 (my humble surname). In slang, 犯贱 means acting annoyingly.

examples.hanzi: 这些东西卖得太贱了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōngxi mài de tài jiàn le.
examples.english: These things are being sold too cheaply.

examples.hanzi: 人不分贵贱，都应该受到尊重。
examples.pinyin: Rén bù fēn guì jiàn, dōu yīnggāi shòudào zūnzhòng.
examples.english: People, high or low, all deserve respect.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
厂 (cliff, shelter) — a building radical, as in 厅 hall, 厨 kitchen, 厕 toilet.
夏 (xià) shares the rhyme of shà, only a loose sound clue.

example.hanzi: 这座大厦有五十层楼那么高。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò dàshà yǒu wǔshí céng lóu nàme gāo.
example.english: This building is as tall as fifty floors.
example.fact: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai, completed in 2010, stands 828 meters (2,717 feet) tall, making it the tallest building in the world. Its design was inspired by the geometric patterns of a desert flower, and its structure tapers as it rises to reduce wind loads at the top.

examples.hanzi: 那座大厦是这个城市最高的建筑。
examples.pinyin: Nà zuò dàshà shì zhège chéngshì zuì gāo de jiànzhù.
examples.english: That tower is the tallest building in this city.

examples.hanzi: 我们公司在市中心的一座大厦里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī zài shì zhōngxīn de yí zuò dàshà lǐ.
examples.english: Our company is in a building in the city center.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person's precedent or example; also in 他 he, 做 do.
列 (liè) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 烈 liè and 裂 liè.
夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.

example.hanzi: 每个规则都有例外。
example.pinyin: měi gè guīzé dōu yǒu lìwài.
example.english: Every rule has an exception.
example.fact: The platypus is one of only five living species of monotremes — mammals that lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young. Discovered by European naturalists in the late 18th century, it was initially dismissed as a hoax because it broke the rule that mammals give birth to live offspring.

examples.hanzi: 今天大家都到了,只有小王是例外。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān dàjiā dōu dào le, zhǐyǒu Xiǎo Wáng shì lìwài.
examples.english: Everyone arrived today, with Xiao Wang being the only exception.

examples.hanzi: 这条规定没有例外,请大家遵守。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo guīdìng méiyǒu lìwài, qǐng dàjiā zūnshǒu.
examples.english: There are no exceptions to this rule, so please follow it.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — marks weather, as in 雷 thunder, 雪 snow, 雾 fog; 震 is a quake, as when thunder shakes the ground.
辰 (chén) hints at the sound: 震 zhèn is close to 振 zhèn, which shares it.
扌 (hand) — shaking by force; also in 摇 shake, 推 push.
感 (gǎn) gives a close sound; 憾 hàn shares it and sounds exactly like 撼.

example.hanzi: 那场地震震撼了整个城市。
example.pinyin: nà chǎng dìzhèn zhènhàn le zhěnggè chéngshì.
example.english: That earthquake shook the entire city.
example.fact: The 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile, with a magnitude of 9.5, remains the most powerful earthquake ever recorded by modern seismographs. It triggered tsunamis that caused damage as far away as Hawaii, Japan, and the Philippines.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影的画面太震撼了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng de huàmiàn tài zhènhàn le.
examples.english: The visuals in this movie are so stunning.

examples.hanzi: 看到那么大的瀑布,我心里很震撼。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào nàme dà de pùbù, wǒ xīnli hěn zhènhàn.
examples.english: Seeing such a huge waterfall, I was deeply awed.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and rivers: 河, 海, 湖; 洛 is the name of a river, now used for sound in foreign names.
各 (gè) gives the sound luò: same part in 路 lù, 落 luò and 络 luò.
囗 (enclosure) — here a mat; oldest form shows a person 大 lying on a mat, "to rely on", later "cause". 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn and 烟 yān.

example.hanzi: 海洛因是一种非常危险的毒品。
example.pinyin: hǎiluòyīn shì yī zhǒng fēicháng wēixiǎn de dúpǐn.
example.english: Heroin is a very dangerous drug.
example.fact: Heroin was first synthesized in 1874 by chemist C.R. Alder Wright, and starting in 1898 the German company Bayer marketed it commercially as a cough suppressant and non-addictive alternative to morphine — a claim that proved tragically wrong once its highly addictive nature became clear.

examples.hanzi: 警察在车上发现了一包海洛因。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài chē shàng fāxiànle yì bāo hǎiluòyīn.
examples.english: The police found a package of heroin in the car.

examples.hanzi: 海洛因会让人上瘾,毁掉一个人的生活。
examples.pinyin: Hǎiluòyīn huì ràng rén shàngyǐn, huǐdiào yí gè rén de shēnghuó.
examples.english: Heroin is addictive and can ruin a person's life.
